qs.q: A 45-year-old man presents with recurrent urinary tract infections, low back pain, and perineal discomfort lasting several months. Routine urine cultures are consistently negative for identifiable uropathogens, and no proven therapy is available. What is the most likely diagnosis?
qs.e: Chronic nonbacterial prostatitis / chronic pelvic pain syndrome accounts for 90-95% of cases and presents with symptoms without an identifiable uropathogen. Acute and chronic bacterial prostatitis have clearly cultured bacterial pathogens.

qs.q: A 52-year-old woman describes her chronic low back pain as traveling down her leg, accompanied by a sudden shooting sensation resembling high-voltage current. Which descriptive quality of pain has this patient reported?
qs.e: Electric-shock like is a recognized qualitative descriptor for neuropathic pain reported by patients during clinical assessment. Throbbing and dull are typical descriptors used for musculoskeletal or nociceptive pain rather than nerve irritation.

qs.q: A 50-year-old man presents with low back pain, recurrent urinary tract infections, and dysuria. Prostatic secretions reveal leukocytes, but repeated urine cultures yield no identifiable uropathogen. What is the most likely category of his condition?
qs.e: Chronic nonbacterial prostatitis (or chronic pelvic pain syndrome) accounts for the vast majority of prostatitis cases and presents with local symptoms and leukocytes without an identifiable uropathogen. Chronic bacterial prostatitis, conversely, consistently demonstrates documented recurrent urinary tract infections from bacterial agents.
